ここ二か月は主にこの本にかかりっきり。本体は780ページ、注と索引を入れると全部で1000ページという大作。
これだけ長くかつテーマも「啓蒙主義」ということになると、読み切るには時間がかかる。必然的に最初の部分の印象がどうも弱くなってくる。
なぜ読んだかといわれると、john grayや福井義高氏の作品を読んでいて、どうもこの啓蒙主義こそがフランス革命やロシア革命並びに現代のsocial justice warriorsの問題の根源のようであるとの認識が徐々に強まってきたためだろうか。
いうまでもなく本書の登場人物は教科書に出てくるような有名人からそれほど知られていない人物まで多岐にわたる。それぞれについて、原典からの引用という形で議論が展開される。悲しいかな、その議論の展開の正邪を判断するだけの知識は持ち合わせていない。著者の議論の展開を追っていくのがやっと。

Book overview

Pragmatism: A New Name for Some Old Ways of Thinking is a philosophical work by the American philosopher and psychologist William James. Originally published in 1907, the book is a collection of lectures that James delivered at the Lowell Institute in Boston in 1906. In this book, James introduces the concept of pragmatism, which he defines as a method of approaching philosophical questions by examining their practical implications. He argues that philosophical ideas should be judged based on their usefulness and practicality, rather than their abstract truth or coherence. James also discusses the history of philosophy and the various philosophical schools of thought that have emerged over time. He critiques the idealism of philosophers like Plato and Immanuel Kant, arguing that their focus on abstract concepts and ideals is disconnected from the realities of human experience.

About the Author

Svetlana Alexievich was born in Ivano-Frankivsk, Ukraine, in 1948 and has spent most of her life in the Soviet Union and present-day Belarus, with prolonged periods of exile in Western Europe. Starting out as a journalist, she developed her own nonfiction genre, which gathers a chorus of voices to describe a specific historical moment. Her works include War’s Unwomanly Face (1985), Last Witnesses (1985), Zinky Boys (1990), Voices from Chernobyl (1997), and Secondhand Time (2013). She has won many international awards, including the 2015 Nobel Prize in Literature “for her polyphonic writings, a monument to suffering and courage in our time.”
